title: City-center Liffey and Royal Canal are absent from the baked terrain.water layer
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:288-290 chains all relation member geometries into ONE LineString: `for m in el.get("members", []):` / `for g in m.get("geometry", []):` / `geoms.append(Point(*transformer.transform(g["lon"], g["lat"])))`; polygonize (line 300) then drops it: `if ls is None or len(ls.coords) < 4 or not ls.is_valid:` -> `return None`. Verified against the committed asset: no polygon in terrain.water intersects board tiles x 13.7-19.5 x y 16.6-17.6 (the Heuston->O'Connell quays stretch of the Liffey); water-blue pixels in that band of docs/captures/dublin-map-spike/dublin_baywide_1in6.png = 0.5%, vs 34.5% in the docks segment (x 19.5-25.0). Along the Royal Canal (Portobello -6.2653,53.3253 -> Crossguns -6.2902,53.3627) the nearest water polygon is 0.72-0.99 tiles away; the canal band (tiles 13-21 x 14-22) renders 1.13% water.
detail: Spec layer list requires 'terrain (the Liffey, ... Royal Canal ...)'. The committed snapshot's water layer has a ~4 km gap across the city quays and no canal water along the Royal Canal.
recommended_fix: Re-bake water: assemble waterway=riverbank/canal relations as proper multipolygons (polygonize member rings separately, not chained) so the quays Liffey and canals survive polygonize().

title: Dublin Bay is not water in the asset: open bay renders canvas paper, intertidal flats classified as park green
evidence: Query line 103 `way["natural"="coastline"]({bbox});` and classification line 432 `if nat == "coastline" or ww == "riverbank" or nat == "water" or ww == "canal" or ww == "dock":` rely on polygonizing OPEN coastline ways. Measured on the committed asset/renders: the bay-east half of dublin_baywide_1in6.png (tiles x 26-40, y 10-24) is 0.4% water-blue, 11.2% park-green, 0.7% beach; the single largest park polygon (11.79 tiles^2, bounds 26.0,10.1 -> 32.8,15.9) sits on the North Bull Island/Dollymouth intertidal flats, where the render is 36.4% green, 0.3% water; mid-bay tile (33.2,20.7) samples exactly canvas (237,226,200).
detail: Spec layer says 'Dublin Bay/coastline'; the committed asset's water layer contains no open-bay polygon, and OSM wetland/sand flats are misclassified into terrain.park.
recommended_fix: Bake the sea explicitly: close the coastline against the board edge (or draw water as the base layer) and query natural=sand/mudflat separately so flats stop landing in park. Record supersession if the paper bay is the user-approved look.

title: osmnx (the spec's named extraction tool) is not used; pinned Overpass QL + shapely/pyproj instead
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py docstring: 'Note on tooling: the briefing names osmnx for the street graph. osmnx's / Overpass query construction and cache keys are version-dependent (not / pin-able), so this tool pins the Overpass QL itself (same pipeline shape: / OSM query -> street ways -> simplified geometry) for a reproducible bake.'
detail: Spec step 1 says 'Tool: osmnx (Python) for the street graph + layers'. Substitution is documented and serves hard rule 2 (deterministic bake pins inputs); pipeline shape is preserved.
recommended_fix: None for the spike; note the substitution in the follow-up integration spec so it does not assume osmnx artifacts.

title: Board dimensions hardcoded in both tools instead of read from data/balance.json map.*
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:72-75: `# Board size (data/balance.json map.*): the camera fits this into 1280x720.` / `BOARD_W_TILES = 40` / `BOARD_H_TILES = 30` / `TILE_PX = 26`; tools/render_dublin_preview.py:30: `TILE_PX = 26          # data/balance.json map.tile_px`; data/balance.json:75-79: `"map": { "w_tiles": 40, "h_tiles": 30, "tile_px": 26 }`.
detail: Spec step 3 fits the projection to 'the board size (map.* in balance.json)'. The tools restate 40/30/26 as literals — silent desync risk if map.* is tuned.
recommended_fix: Load map.w_tiles/h_tiles/tile_px from data/balance.json (fail-fast on mismatch) in both tools instead of restating the constants.

title: Full 'local' residential street layer kept beyond the spec's arterial-only simplification
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:115 `way["highway"="residential"]({bbox});`; line 160 `LOCAL_MIN_LEN_M = 45.0   # drop residential ways shorter than this (post-simplify)`; lines 421-425 `if hw == "residential":` / `# drop the tiny street fragments — the anti-noise ask` / `if s.length >= LOCAL_MIN_LEN_M:` / `local_lines.append(line)`. Committed asset streets.local = 12,422 ways (streets.arterial = 9,515).
detail: Spec layer list says 'street graph SIMPLIFIED (arterials ... — merge tiny residential streets)'; the asset instead keeps 12,422 residential ways as a separate 'local' layer, dropping (not merging) sub-45 m fragments.
recommended_fix: Keep — it supports the settled streets-constrain-pipes ruling and was visible in the approved gallery; carry the layer forward explicitly in the follow-up spec.
